items.h: Mason Rudolph to start for Steelers in Week 12
items.s: Mason Rudolph has been named the starting QB for the Steelers for Friday's game against the Broncos. The Steelers have made the decision to bench Aaron Rodgers. Rudolph will attempt to revamp the Steelers offense.

Rudolph will start Friday's game against the Broncos, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix reports. In a stunning move late Tuesday night, the Steelers benched Aaron Rodgers following two straight losses to the Bengals and Eagles, where the offense didn't play well at all, as Rodgers averaged a paltry 5.1 yards per attempt. The Steelers will see if Rudolph can provide a spark for 6-4 Pittsburgh. Rudolph has made 19 career regular-season starts and has averaged 6.6 yards per attempt with a 30:22 TD:INT on 742 pass attempts.

items.h: Mason Rudolph to Start on Friday vs. Broncos
items.s: The Pittsburgh Steelers are shockingly benching future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who will not be active for the Black Friday game in Week 12 against the visiting Denver Broncos, according to the NFL Network's Cameron Wolfe. It means that backup Mason Rudolph will be thrust into the starting role as the Steelers look to put an end to a two-game losing streak that has dropped them to 6-4 on the year. Although the 31-year-old may not be much more than a game manager under center as he replaces a living legend, he will immediately become attractive as a waiver-wire pickup in superflex leagues for potentially the rest of the 2026 season. items.h: Directs final drive of blowout loss
items.s: Rudolph completed one of three pass attempts for two yards and rushed once for nine yards in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals. After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.

Rudolph is active for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports. Rudolph has emerged as the Steelers' preferred backup quarterback behind starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers coming out of the preseason. Through each of Pittsburgh's first seven contests, Rudolph has suited up, while both Will Howard and Drew Allar have been inactive. Howard is the Steelers' emergency No. 3 quarterback and will be called upon to play only in the event that both Rodgers and Rudolph are forced to exit Sunday's game.

items.h: Mason Rudolph listed as Steelers' QB2 on Week 1 depth chart
items.s: The Steelers have listed Mason Rudolph as their QB2 on the Week 1 depth chart. Will Howard is No. 3 and rookie Drew Allar is No. 4 on the opening depth chart as the Steelers kept all four quarterbacks on the roster.

Rudolph did not play in Thursday night's preseason finale against the Bills. Rudolph has likely already secured the backup quarterback role behind Aaron Rodgers to start the 2026 regular season. Thursday night's contest once again saw a half of Will Howard (head) and a half of Drew Allar at quarterback, leaving Rudolph to rest with Rodgers as they await the regular season.

Rudolph will not play in Friday's preseason game against the Jets, Chris Adamski of TribLive.com reports. Coach Mike McCarthy said Wednesday that he "saw what I need to see from Mason last week," implying the veteran quarterback has a place on the team for 2026. Friday's game will be dominated by Will Howard and Drew Allar, one of whom is presumably the Steelers' quarterback of the future once Aaron Rodgers retires.

items.h: Mason Rudolph Sharp in Preseason Start
items.s: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph completed 10 of 11 pass attempts for 93 yards in a 28-9 preseason victory over the Green Bay Packers. Rudolph got off to a rocky start, taking two sacks over his first four snaps, but quickly settled in and led the offense down the field on its second possession. Although the Steelers were unable to score after an offensive holding penalty nullified a three-yard rushing touchdown by Lew Nichols, Rudolph displayed early chemistry with rookie wideout Germie Bernard and several other pass-catchers throughout the drive. items.h: Mason Rudolph Dominating Steelers' Backup Competition
items.s: The Pittsburgh Steelers spent a third and a sixth-round pick at quarterback over the course of the past two drafts, but according to beat reporter Alan Saunders, the battle for the primary backup job behind Aaron Rodgers has been dominated by veteran Mason Rudolph. Saunders lists both Will Howard and Drew Allar among his losers of the second week of Steelers training camp, with them all but handing the competition to Rudolph. While Rudolph himself has done little to stand out, Howard has reportedly been unable to close the gap that looked to be tightening during OTAs, making too many errors to overcome a limited skill set.
